what_happened: The job to lift per-agent budget and timeout caps in athena.toml was refused at admission. The edit raised the stage caps so they added up to $47.00 (reader, every planning round, producer, verifier), but the job-level budget job_usd stayed at $40.00, $7.00 short. The job ended failed before any work started. No acceptance criterion was judged and no check failed. Admission refused the config as a whole.
cause: The job-level budget and the per-stage caps are separate numbers in one file. An admission rule enforces that the budget covers the sum of the caps. Neither the reading nor the plan is shown this rule or computes the sum, so a request to lift caps is accepted as is. It is only found when admission refuses the job. This is related to, but not the same as, the existing budget classes, which concern remaining budget after earlier attempts, not a config edit that breaks its own invariant.
prevention: When a reading is accepted for any change touching [budget] or agent cap fields in athena.toml, run the admission budget-versus-caps check on the proposed config. Do this at reading and plan time, and when it fails, report the required job_usd (here at least $47.00) and make raising job_usd a required deliverable and criterion. Ideally add a command that takes proposed cap values and prints the minimum job_usd needed.
proposed_request: Raise the per-agent budget and timeout caps in athena.toml as intended by the earlier request (job 20261104-140950-gzp9), and raise [budget] job_usd in the same change so it is at least the sum of the reader, every planning round, producer and verifier caps. With the caps as they stood in that attempt, the sum is $47.00, so job_usd must be at least $47.00. Acceptance: athena.toml parses and passes admission, job_usd is no less than the computed sum of the stage caps, and no file other than athena.toml (and any test that reads these values) is changed.
